phrases.en: Nice to meet you! I just arrived from Taiwan.
phrases.zh: 很高興認識你！我剛從台灣來。
phrases.note: 最基本的自我介紹開場白。用於第一次見面的任何場合。

phrases.en: Could you help me with something?
phrases.note: 萬用求助句型。語氣比 'Help me' 更有禮貌。

phrases.en: I'm here on a working holiday visa.
phrases.zh: 我持打工度假簽證來的。
phrases.note: 入境時或認識新朋友時常用。簡潔說明你的身份。

phrases.en: How do you like Canada so far?
phrases.zh: 你到目前為止覺得加拿大怎麼樣？
phrases.note: 別人可能會問你這個問題。也可以反問對方。

phrases.en: I'm still getting used to everything here.
phrases.zh: 我還在適應這裡的一切。
phrases.note: 誠實且自然的回答。Canadians 會理解並給你鼓勵。

dialogues.title: At the Immigration Counter
dialogues.sit: You just landed at Vancouver International Airport. You are going through immigration.
lines: Good afternoon. Welcome to Canada. May I see your passport, please?
Good afternoon. Here is my passport.
Thank you. What is the purpose of your visit?
I am here on a working holiday visa. I plan to work and travel in Canada.
How long do you plan to stay?
The duration of my visa is twelve months.
Do you have an address in Canada?
Yes, I have accommodation in Vancouver. Here is the address.
Do you have anything to declare?
No, I do not have anything to declare.
Alright. Welcome to Canada. Enjoy your stay!
dialogues.tp: Now try again, but this time your visa duration is TWO years and you are staying in Toronto.
dialogues.tn: 重點觀察學生是否能正確說出 'working holiday visa' 和 'duration'。th 音 (the, this, that) 出現頻率高，可在此對話後做 Pronunciation Spotlight。

dialogues.title: Meeting Your Roommate
dialogues.sit: You arrive at your new accommodation. Your Canadian roommate opens the door.
lines: Hey! You must be the new roommate. I'm Jamie. Come on in!
Hi Jamie! Nice to meet you. I am [your name]. You can call me [nickname].
Nice to meet you too! Where are you from?
I am from Taiwan. I just arrived today.
Oh cool! How was your flight?
It was long, but I am happy to be here. I have a lot of jet lag though!
Ha, I bet! Let me show you around. This is the kitchen, and your room is down the hall.
Thank you! This accommodation looks really nice.
Thanks! Oh, and just so you know — we usually take turns doing the dishes. Pretty casual here.
No problem! That sounds very friendly. I am still getting used to everything.
You will love it here. Canadians are pretty polite and laid-back. Let me know if you need anything!
Thank you, Jamie. I really appreciate it.
dialogues.tp: Now try again, but your roommate's name is Alex and you arrived yesterday (not today).
dialogues.tn: 觀察學生是否能自然使用 nickname 和 casual 語氣。注意 'nice to meet you' 的語調是否自然。

dialogues.title: Asking for Directions at the Airport
dialogues.sit: You just cleared customs and need to find the bus to downtown.
lines: Excuse me, could you help me with something?
Of course! What do you need?
Where can I find the bus to downtown Vancouver?
Sure! Go straight, then turn left. You will see the transit signs. Follow them to the bus stop.
Thank you! How much is the bus fare?
It is about three dollars. You can use a credit card or buy a transit pass.
Great. And where can I exchange currency?
There is an exchange counter near the arrival gate. It is on your right.
Thank you so much. You are very friendly!
No problem! Welcome to Canada. Enjoy your stay!
dialogues.tp: Now try again, but ask about the train (SkyTrain) instead of the bus.
dialogues.tn: 核心句型 'Could you help me with something?' — 確認學生的語調是上揚的（禮貌問句）。

dialogues.title: Taking a Taxi to Your Accommodation
dialogues.sit: You decide to take a taxi because you have heavy luggage.
lines: Hi! Can you take me to this address, please?
Sure, hop in! Is this your first time in Canada?
Yes! I just arrived today. I am here on a working holiday visa.
That is awesome! Where are you from?
I am from Taiwan. I am very excited to be here.
You will love Vancouver. It is very multicultural. The fare will be about thirty dollars.
That sounds good. Do you accept credit cards?
Yes, we accept all major cards. Here we are! Let me help you with your luggage.
Thank you! You are very polite.
No problem. Good luck with your new adventure!
dialogues.tp: Now try again, but this time you are going to a hostel downtown and need to ask about the estimated travel time.
dialogues.tn: 練習數字表達 (thirty dollars) 和禮貌用語。

dialogues.title: Meeting a Canadian Neighbor
dialogues.sit: You are checking your mailbox and your neighbor starts talking to you.
lines: Hi there! I have not seen you before. Did you just move in?
Yes! I moved in yesterday. I am [your name]. Nice to meet you!
Welcome to the building! I am Sarah. Where are you from?
I am from Taiwan. I am here on a working holiday.
How exciting! How do you like Canada so far?
I love it! Everyone is so friendly. But I am still getting used to the cold weather!
Ha! Yeah, you will get used to it. If you ever need anything, just knock on my door. I am in unit 305.
That is so kind of you! Thank you, Sarah.
Anytime! By the way, there is a great grocery store two blocks from here. I can show you this weekend if you want.
That would be great! I do not know the neighborhood yet.
dialogues.tp: Now try again, but this time Sarah invites you for coffee instead of showing you the grocery store.
dialogues.tn: 觀察 small talk 的自然度。學生是否能用 'How do you like Canada so far?' 自然回應。

speaking.q: Do you prefer living in a big city or a small town?
speaking.h: Answer: I prefer living in a ___ because...

speaking.q: Have you ever traveled to a country where you did not speak the language?
speaking.h: Answer: Yes, I have. / No, I have not. One time I...

speaking.q: What are you most excited about for your time in Canada? Start with: I am most excited about...
speaking.h: Try to give at least two reasons.

speaking.q: What do you think is the biggest difference between Taiwan and Canada? Start with: I think the biggest difference is...
speaking.h: Think about food, weather, culture, or people.

speaking.q: If a friend from Taiwan is planning a working holiday in Canada, what three things would you tell them to prepare?
speaking.h: Speak freely for at least 30 seconds.

culture.title: Tim Hortons — Canada's Coffee Culture
culture.tz: Tim Hortons — 加拿大咖啡文化
culture.photo: Photo: A Tim Hortons store front with the red and white logo. A customer holds a coffee cup and a box of Timbits (donut holes).
culture.notes: Tim Hortons is the most popular coffee chain in Canada. Most Canadians call it 'Timmies.' A 'double-double' means coffee with two creams and two sugars. Timbits are small round donuts — great for sharing! Tim Hortons is often the first place new arrivals visit.
qs: Do you have a favorite coffee shop in Taiwan? What do you usually order?
In Taiwan, what drink or shop is as popular as Tim Hortons in Canada?
Would you like to try a 'double-double'? Why or why not?

culture.title: Canadian Greetings — 'Sorry' Culture
culture.tz: 加拿大式問候 — 道歉文化
culture.photo: Photo: Two Canadians meeting on the street, smiling and waving casually. A humorous sign saying 'Sorry, eh!'
culture.notes: Canadians say 'sorry' a lot — even when it is not their fault! If someone bumps into YOU, they might say sorry. 'Eh' is a Canadian word added to the end of sentences, like 'Nice day, eh?' It is like saying 'right?' in English or '對吧?' in Chinese.
qs: In Taiwan, do people apologize a lot? Compare it to Canada.
Try using 'eh' at the end of a sentence. How does it feel?
What greeting style do you prefer — formal or casual? Why?
